text: Which probabilistic data structure provides space-efficient, approximate set-membership testing and underlies k-mer counting tools such as jellyfish?
explanation: Bloom filters are explicitly named as the space-efficient, approximate set-membership structure used by jellyfish for k-mer counting. MinHash instead estimates Jaccard similarity between sets (e.g., for genome distance estimation), Count-Min Sketch estimates item frequencies rather than membership, and a standard hash table with open addressing gives exact membership testing at higher memory cost, not approximate.
